audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side marked levels 1 and 4-5 as even and gave Jayce both item stages, contradicting whys[0], whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5].
audit.why: Shock Blast through the Acceleration Gate out-ranges everything Gwen has from level 1, so 1 through 4-5 are all his; level 6 is stated as her fight; and whys[5] and whys[6] describe both item stages as even because he can poke-and-gate to avoid the duel he loses.
audit.corrected: Jayce / Jayce / Jayce / Jayce / Gwen / Skill / Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Look for the gap when his Shock Blast is on cooldown' and 'bait his Thundering Blow' with no numbers on either.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16/14/12/10/8/6 and Thundering Blow 20/18/16/14/12/10, against Hallowed Mist at 22s. At rank 1 a spent Shock Blast is a 16-second window; by max rank it is six, shorter than a single Snip Snip! rotation. The window you are told to hunt closes as the game goes on, which is the whole reason to force the fight at your level-6 spike.
audit.corrected: mid, late, whys[2] and wants.you[0] now carry the numbers and the shrinking-window point.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mercury Cannon (R), his stance swap, is never named and never identified as an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Mercury Cannon carries the autoReset flag on a flat 6s cooldown. The swap animation into hammer form is the tell that a Thundering Blow knockback is about to land on your E-dash - reading the swap rather than the hammer cast is what lets you hold Skip 'n Slash for after the knockback instead of losing it to one.
audit.corrected: mid and wants.foe[1] now name the Mercury Cannon swap reset as the tell.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still rough, you're a melee with no mist eating ranged poke pre-spike. But level 6 flips it. With Needlework up and Hallowed Mist available, drop W on top of yourself to become untargetable to his poke, then E-dash in with the on-hit range bonus and snip him while your ability healing tops you back up. Chain R to slow him so he can't simply gate away, and if you hit him with E you get most of the cooldown back to stay on him. Bait his hammer-form Thundering Blow before you commit so the knockback is wasted, not saving him.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still rough, you're a melee with no mist eating ranged poke pre-spike. But level 6 flips it. With Needlework up and Hallowed Mist available, drop W on top of yourself to become untargetable to his poke, then E-dash in with the on-hit range bonus and snip him while your healing tops you back up. Chain R so he cannot gate away, and hitting him with E refunds most of the dash. Watch the Mercury Cannon swap, not the hammer cast — it is a 6s auto reset and it is your only warning that a 20s Thundering Blow knockback is coming, so bait it before you commit.

edits.before: It stays a knife's edge. The instant you touch him inside your mist, Snip Snip!'s %-max-HP damage and its true-damage center snip plus your all-in delete him, he's squishy and builds no lifesteal to out-trade your sustain. The problem is a fed Jayce never lets you touch him: he pokes from gate range and walks backward on his gate speed. Look for the gap when his Shock Blast is on cooldown, use mist to cross the poke, and let your team eat the harass so you only need to land one E-dash combo.
edits.after: It stays a knife's edge. The instant you touch him inside your mist, Snip Snip!'s %-max-HP damage and its true-damage center snip plus your all-in delete him, he's squishy and builds no lifesteal to out-trade your sustain. The problem is a fed Jayce never lets you touch him. His Shock Blast window shrinks from 16s at rank 1 to 6s at max, so the gap you are hunting closes as the game runs — use mist to cross the poke early, let your team eat the harass, and land the one E-dash combo before that window is gone.

edits.before: You can start contesting with Q and E, but he still out-ranges you and his gate mobility resets the spacing before you arrive.
edits.after: You can contest with Q and E, but his 16s Shock Blast still out-ranges you and gate mobility resets the spacing before you arrive.

edits.before: Survive levels 1-3 by last-hitting at the tip of your range, out of Shock Blast's empowered poke, until you have Hallowed Mist
edits.after: Survive levels 1-3 last-hitting at the tip of your range, out of a 16s Shock Blast's empowered poke, until you have Hallowed Mist

edits.before: Hold hammer-form Thundering Blow to knock you away the moment you E in, then gate-speed out of your combo
edits.after: Swap with Mercury Cannon into a 20s Thundering Blow to knock you away as you E in, then gate-speed out

notes: Names are correct and the prose is second-person. Fixes: (1) the chart gave Gwen nothing and marked levels 1 and 4-5 even while giving Jayce both item stages - the reverse of whys[0], whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5]. Corrected to Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Gwen/Skill/Skill, which matches the 45.82% win rate: a lane you lose outright until your level-6 mist window, then hold even. (2) The page tells you to 'look for the gap when his Shock Blast is on cooldown' without the number. Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 and drops to 6s at rank 6, and Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1 - so the window the page sends you looking for shrinks from sixteen seconds to six as the lane goes on, which is why the level-6 all-in has to happen early rather than being saved. (3) Mercury Cannon (R) is his stance swap on a flat 6s and it is an auto-attack RESET: the swap wind-up, not the hammer cast, is the tell that Thundering Blow is coming. That is never mentioned and it is the read that decides whether your E-dash gets knocked back.
